This is the most informative pair I have seen: ligand 2 derives to jnk3~0.06, which is several times higher than anything else in this pool, and its distinguishing feature is unambiguous - an N-aryl carboxamide whose aniline carries a 1H-pyrazol-3-yl at the para position (C(=O)Nc2ccc(-c3ccn[nH]3)cc2). That is a hinge-binding azole presented on an anilide, exactly the arrangement real JNK3 amide series use. Ligand 1 is the inactive azetidine-piperazinium. Crossover would only include ligand 2 half the time and would join it to a random half of ligand 1, so instead I will rebuild ligand 2 feature directly on my working molecule, which is deterministic. Cut non-ring bond 11-12 to remove the protonated piperazine and graft the whole pyrazolylphenyl-carboxamide unit onto the azetidine C3 in its place. That removes the charge that was capping QED at 0.63 and installs the only motif in this pool with measurable activity.

Motif transplanted and the charge is gone - QED 0.634 -> 0.712, SA 3.80 -> 2.54. The remaining problem is flexibility: 8 rotatable bonds, almost all of them in the isopropoxyethyl tail on the sulfonyl (atoms 0-5), plus ~100 Da of dead weight. Cut the non-ring S-CH2 bond 6-5 and put a methyl there, giving the methanesulfonyl azetidine-3-carboxanilide at ~320 Da with 4 rotatable bonds and LogP near 0.8. That leaves the pyrazolylphenyl-amide pharmacophore as the dominant feature of a compact, highly accessible molecule.
